ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in Figure (1), a coil with $N=200$ turns (only 2 turns are drawn in the figure) has a resistance of $r=2\Omega$. Its two ends are connected to a resistor of $R=48\Omega$. There is a magnetic field pointing into the paper within the coil. The magnetic flux through the coil changes according to the pattern shown in Figure (2).

1. Determine the direction of the current passing through the resistor $R$.
2. Calculate the induced electromotive force $E$ generated by the coil.
3. Calculate the voltage $U$ across the resistor $R$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure (1), a coil with N = 200 turns (only 2 turns are drawn in the figure) has a resistance of r = 2Ω. Its two ends are connected to a resistor of R = 48Ω. There is a magnetic field pointing into the paper within the coil. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: Figure (1) shows a vertical external resistor R on the left, with terminal a at the top and terminal b at the bottom. The resistor is connected by wires to the two ends of a coil on the right. Inside the coil, the magnetic field is represented by crosses, so it points into the paper. Figure (2) shows the magnetic flux Φ increasing linearly with time: it is 0.010 Wb at t = 0 and reaches 0.015 Wb at t = 0.10 s. Reasoning: The magnetic flux into the paper is increasing, so by Lenz’s law the induced current must create a magnetic field out of the paper to oppose that increase. By the right-hand rule, this corresponds to a counterclockwise induced current around the coil as viewed in the diagram. Following the lead connections shown in Figure (1), the current through the external resistor R is from a to b. The rate of change of magnetic flux is ΔΦ/Δt = (0.015 − 0.010) / 0.10 = 0.05 Wb/s. With N = 200 turns, the induced electromotive force is E = NΔΦ/Δt = 200 × 0.05 = 10 V. The total circuit resistance is R + r = 48 Ω + 2 Ω = 50 Ω. The circuit current is I = E/(R + r) = 10/50 = 0.20 A. Therefore the voltage across the external resistor is U = IR = 0.20 × 48 = 9.6 V.
